description: A request to buy service credits, raised by a Rest deployment. DRAFT means requested and unpaid; SUBMITTED means money has been received and the credits are claimable by the app. The draft-to-submitted step is the whole point: only a person, or a payment gateway's own script, can submit, so nothing a tenant application says can make credits real on its own. Reports filtering on docstatus will not count drafts as revenue, which a status field on a single doctype cannot guarantee.

fields.label: Purchase Reference
fields.description: The reference the customer quotes when they pay, and how the operator FINDS this proposal. Required: a purchase that cannot be referenced cannot be matched to a payment, so the proposal would be unmatchable rather than merely hard to find.

fields.label: Rest Instance
fields.description: The Rest deployment that asked. A Link, so the identifier resolves to a record carrying the deployment's name and activity.

fields.label: Channel
fields.description: SMS and email credit are separate balances and are never interchangeable.

fields.label: Units
fields.description: Service units requested: SMS segments or email messages. An integer, never a float.

fields.label: Amount (minor units)
fields.description: What the deployment quoted, in the currency's MINOR units. A settler may correct it: a payment that arrives for a different amount is a fact about money that moved, and refusing it would strand a real payment. The settled amount wins and the difference is recorded.

fields.label: Unit Price (micros)
fields.description: The price this purchase was quoted at, in millionths of a major unit. Pricing is pinned when the app raises the request and never re-priced.

fields.label: Settlement
fields.description: Filled in when the money has been received. This is the part the Rest app can never do for itself.

fields.label: Payment Document Type
fields.description: Pick the doctype first (Payment Entry, Sales Invoice, Journal Entry...), then the document. A Dynamic Link needs both halves, which is why it is visible.

fields.label: Payment Document
fields.description: The payment this settlement is for. This field turns 'money was received' from a claim into something the books already agree with -- before it existed, nothing anywhere checked that a payment had happened at all.

fields.label: Expires At
fields.description: When an unpaid proposal stops being claimable. Set by the deployment and stored here, so both sides agree on the deadline.

fields.label: Settled By
fields.description: Who submitted this settlement. On a gateway path this is a script's user rather than a person; either way it is recorded, because 'who made this claimable' must always be answerable.

fields.label: Settlement Note
fields.description: Anything the settler must record: a cash receipt number, a gateway reference, or why an EXPIRED proposal was settled late.

fields.label: Quote Variance (minor)
fields.description: Settled amount minus quoted amount. Non-zero means the money that arrived differs from the quote, which is recorded rather than hidden.

name: Rest Credit Proposal
